title: Pre-conciliar tradition cannot be the certain foundation of faith in Scripture
source_text: XXXVII. Neque hic recurri potest ad traditionem aliquam Ecclesiae, quasi ante Concilia quae librorum sacrorum numerum definierunt, Ecclesiae traditio fuerit fidei de Scriptura fundamentum. Nam Pontificii volunt traditionem esse quidem medium quo Ecclesia utitur in dijudicandis eis quae fidei sunt, attamen traditionem dubiam esse volunt, non minus quam libros Scripturae, nec esse certum fidei fundamentum, antequam publico Ecclesiae judicio probata fuerit.
pass_a_gloss: Nor can one here have recourse to some tradition of the Church, as if before the Councils that defined the number of the sacred books the tradition of the Church had been the foundation of faith concerning Scripture. For the Pontificii want tradition indeed to be a medium which the Church uses in judging those things that belong to faith, yet they want tradition to be doubtful no less than the books of Scripture, and not to be a certain foundation of faith until it has been proved by a public judgment of the Church.
pass_b_english: Nor may one fall back on some Church tradition, as if before the councils that fixed the number of sacred books tradition itself had been the foundation of faith concerning Scripture.

Rome grants that tradition is a means the Church uses in judging matters of faith. Yet on Rome's own terms tradition is as doubtful as the books of Scripture, and is no certain foundation of faith until a public Church judgment has proved it.
